# Appendix A: Platform Capability Inventory {#sec-appendix-inventory .unnumbered}

Beyond the summary of @sec-platform, the counterfactual and energetics
stack comprises: per-engine `compute_ztcf` / `compute_zvcf` /
drift-control implementations (MuJoCo, Drake, Pinocchio, OpenSim,
MyoSuite, analytic pendulum engines, Simscape bridge) behind the
engine-core contract
([`_dynamics_interface.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/engine_core/_dynamics_interface.py));
the pointwise evaluator with canonical-v2 trajectory input and HDF5
persistence
([`ztcf_zvcf.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/simulation_backends/ztcf_zvcf.py));
a Newton-Euler ZTCF force module with an analytic single-pendulum
validation identity
([`biomechanics/ztcf.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/biomechanics/ztcf.py));
induced-acceleration analyzers
([`induced_acceleration.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/engines/physics_engines/mujoco/python/mujoco_humanoid_golf/rigid_body_dynamics/induced_acceleration.py));
an orchestration layer with capability gating and REST/UI surfaces
([`analysis/orchestrator.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/analysis/orchestrator.py));
MuJoCo inter-segment power flow with per-body energies and
drift/control work decomposition
([`power_flow.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/engines/physics_engines/mujoco/python/mujoco_humanoid_golf/power_flow.py));
engine-agnostic work/power/impulse and system-energy metrics
([`power_work_metrics.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/analysis/power_work_metrics.py),
[`energy_metrics.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/analysis/energy_metrics.py));
conservation monitoring
([`energy_monitor.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/physics/energy_monitor.py));
kinematic-sequence and coordination analytics with plot renderers
([`kinematic_sequence.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/biomechanics/kinematic_sequence.py),
[`coordination_metrics.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/analysis/coordination_metrics.py),
[`_coordination_sequence.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/plotting/renderers/_coordination_sequence.py));
an approved internal research review of the kinematic-sequence metric
([`kinematic_sequence.md`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/docs/assessments/research_reviews/kinematic_sequence.md));
and the MATLAB BASE/ZTCF/DELTA/ZVCF pipeline with per-joint
linear/angular work and power decompositions (@sec-ztcf-variants).

## Known gaps {#sec-appendix-gaps .unnumbered}

| Gap | Consequence for this document |
|---|---|
| Two ZTCF operationalizations (pointwise vs re-simulation) coexist; no Python re-simulation ZTCF | @sec-results uses the pointwise variant only; parity untested (issue #8377) |
| Inter-segment power transfer in the shared layer is joint-power only (MuJoCo) | The Robertson-Winter accounting of @sec-methods lives in the experiment package, pending promotion (issue #8378) |
| `ConservationMonitor` potential energy is first-order approximate | Not used for any number here; energies computed analytically |
| Flexible-shaft strain energy absent from the energy budget | Shaft recoil energy invisible until the shaft rung of @sec-future |
| Proximal-braking-efficiency metric is an open TODO | Deceleration claims here rely on directly computed energies instead |

: Known platform gaps (tracked in issue
[#8378](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/issues/8378)). {#tbl-gaps}

# Appendix B: Reproducibility Guide {#sec-appendix-repro .unnumbered}

From the repository root (Python 3.11+, with `numpy`, `matplotlib`,
`pydantic`, `simpleeval`, `pandas` installed):

```bash
# 1. Run all experiments (E1 sweep, E2 counterfactuals, E4 powers)
python3 -m scripts.research.proximal_distal_energy.run_experiments

# 2. Bounded-actuator sensitivity sweep (E1b, incl. its figure)
python3 -m scripts.research.proximal_distal_energy.e1b_bounded_torque

# 3. Regenerate the remaining figures
python3 -m scripts.research.proximal_distal_energy.make_figures

# 4. Rebuild this document (Quarto + LaTeX)
cd docs/research/proximal_distal_energy_transfer
quarto render proximal_distal_energy_transfer.qmd --to pdf
```

Outputs land in `data/` (JSON + NPZ, with provenance: git SHA,
integrator settings, full parameter values) and `figures/` (PDF). The
experiments are deterministic (fixed-step RK4, no stochastic elements),
so re-running reproduces every number in @sec-results exactly, up to
floating-point environment differences.

# Appendix C: Validation Evidence {#sec-appendix-validation .unnumbered}

The counterfactual stack this document relies on is contract-tested in
CI: the pointwise evaluator reproduces the analytic double-pendulum
ground truth to $10^{-9}$ via the ODE and analytical providers, and
agrees with the independent MuJoCo backend to $10^{-7}$ when that engine
is available
([`test_ztcf_zvcf.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/tests/unit/simulation_backends/test_ztcf_zvcf.py));
drift-plus-control reconstructs the measured acceleration
([`test_counterfactual_experiments.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/tests/acceptance/test_counterfactual_experiments.py));
work-energy-theorem and conservation-law property tests run in CI
([`tests/integration/conservation_laws/`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/tree/main/tests/integration/conservation_laws));
and a cross-engine comparison service produces divergence-annotated
ZTCF/ZVCF panels between backends
([`cross_engine_comparison.md`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/docs/simulation_backends/cross_engine_comparison.md)).
The design guidelines make the drift-control decomposition and
ZTCF/ZVCF availability normative across engines
([`project_design_guidelines.qmd`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/docs/project_design_guidelines.qmd)).
Within this document, the wrist-interface accounting carries its own
internal check: the club's mechanical-energy rate matches the summed
interface powers along the full trajectory (@fig-wristpower, right).

# Appendix D: Model Parameters and Program Definitions {#sec-appendix-params .unnumbered}

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Arm length $l_1$ | 0.75 m | `GolfModelParams.default()` |
| Arm mass $m_1$ | 7.5 kg | both arms lumped |
| Arm COM ratio | 0.45 | $l_{c1} = 0.3375$ m |
| Arm inertia about COM | 0.3516 kg·m² | about hub: 1.2059 kg·m² |
| Club length $l_2$ | 1.0 m | |
| Shaft mass | 0.15 kg | COM ratio 0.43 |
| Clubhead mass | 0.20 kg | point mass at tip |
| Club composite mass $m_2$ | 0.35 kg | $l_{c2} = 0.7557$ m |
| Club inertia about COM | 0.0403 kg·m² | about wrist: 0.2402 kg·m² |
| Plane inclination | 35° | projected gravity 8.033 m/s² |
| Damping (shoulder, wrist) | 0.4, 0.25 N·m·s/rad | viscous |
| Integrator | RK4, $\Delta t = 1$ ms | ODE reference backend |
| Initial state | $\theta_1=-2.2$, $\theta_2=-1.57$ rad, $\dot q = 0$ | top of backswing |
| Shoulder torque $\tau_s$ | 60 / 100 N·m | constant from $t=0$ |
| Wrist drive | +15 N·m from $t_{\mathrm{on}}$ | onset grid 0–0.35 s, step 0.025 |
| Wrist restraint $R$ | 5 / 10 N·m before $t_{\mathrm{on}}$ | restrain-then-drive only |
| Impact | first $\theta_1+\theta_2 = 0$ crossing | valid iff $\theta_1 \le 2.0$ rad |

: Model parameters and experiment constants
(`scripts/research/proximal_distal_energy/`). {#tbl-params}

Data dictionary for the recorded outputs:

- `data/e1_sweep.json` — one row per program: profile, torques, onset,
  impact time, clubhead speed, arm angle at impact (null = invalid),
  plus a provenance block.
- `data/representative_traces.npz` — per representative program:
  `t, q, v, u`, drift/control splits, segment energies, clubhead-speed
  trace, and all interface-power series.
- `data/results_summary.json` — program definitions, impact tuples,
  phase budgets, passive baselines, best/worst rows, provenance.
- `data/e1b_bounded_sweep.json` — the bounded-actuator sweep rows with
  their own provenance block (isometric torques, $\omega_{\max}$
  values).
